tasks.short: Teach safe use and care of classroom equipment

steps.what: Instruct students in safe equipment use and monitor handling throughout the activity

tasks.design: Keep demonstration and continuous supervision with the teacher. Equipment instructions in {DOCS} remain reference material without an assumed reporting task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Safety depends on seeing and responding to how each student handles equipment.
tasks.enabler_now: Accessible reference materials can support demonstration but do not replace supervision.
tasks.still_hard: Anticipating unsafe movements and adjusting assistance immediately.
tasks.human_edge: Patient demonstration and proportionate physical intervention.
tasks.altitude: No change to supervision time or safety responsibility.

evidence.claim: Retaining live equipment instruction and supervision is an E1 design judgement.

assumptions: Boundary is direct instruction and monitoring, excluding equipment procurement and separate lesson preparation.
The teacher observes handling during s1; no automated danger flag or structured behaviour input is assumed.
No new software or ongoing upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: Equipment hazards and individual assistance requirements
research_questions: Which activities require additional qualified supervision?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100; gross and net zero because live instruction and monitoring remain intact.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Provide accessible classroom materials through Braille and sign language

steps.what: Prepare source materials and choose the student's Braille code and accessible output format
Transcribe prepared classroom text into Braille and resolve unsupported notation
Proofread Braille against source meaning and approve the exact accessible classroom material
Interpret classroom materials through sign language and check student understanding

tasks.design: Configure an existing {OTHER} Braille translation tool for prepared text, then retain qualified proofreading against {DOCS}. Sign language interpretation remains live and human; complex notation or unsupported layouts return to manual transcription.
tasks.previous_blocker: Transcription involves repetitive text conversion alongside specialist judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Established rule based Braille translation can reduce typing for supported text.
tasks.still_hard: Tactile layout, notation and faithful signed interpretation require specialist competence.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising whether the student actually understands the material.
tasks.altitude: Some transcription time becomes available for accessible teaching; interpretation responsibility is unchanged.

reach.learn: Applicable Braille conventions and output validation

evidence.claim: Configured Braille translation for supported text with qualified proofreading is an E1 capability assumption; the digest supplies no Braille case or saving.

assumptions: Boundary includes source preparation, Braille transcription, proofreading and signed interpretation; existing accessible output equipment is available.
Teacher produces checked text, language, Braille code and output format in fully retained s1; diagrams and unsupported notation are manually transcribed within s2.
Test native translation settings before custom code. The teacher is qualified to proofread; if a separate specialist is needed, count that labour before adopting.
Two additional hours per 100 baseline hours cover translation settings and sample output checks.
unknowns: Braille code, material complexity and current translation tools
research_questions: Does supported text conversion reduce transcription time after source preparation and proofreading?

incremental.description: Translation settings and sample output maintenance

approvals.approved_version: Exact proofread Braille file and source version; any change voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R87.5; gross12.5 less2 upkeep gives10.5 net. Unsupported layouts may leave no transcription gain and a net loss of2; signing and proofreading do not shrink.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Provide school assistance and supervise shared spaces and bus loading

steps.what: Perform library assistance, hall and cafeteria monitoring, and bus loading and unloading supervision

tasks.design: Keep school assistance and supervision with the teacher. Existing duty schedules in {CALENDAR} provide context without creating an assumed clerical saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: These administrative duties are mainly physical presence and student support.
tasks.enabler_now: Scheduling tools do not remove the need for staffed supervision.
tasks.still_hard: Responding to student needs during crowded transitions.
tasks.human_edge: Situational awareness, reassurance and timely intervention.
tasks.altitude: The duty allocation and time remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Physical school assistance and monitoring remain human in this E1 design judgement.

assumptions: Boundary is carrying out assigned duties, excluding production of the schoolwide rota.
No structured occupancy flag or automated safety decision is introduced; direct observation remains in s1.
No new workflow means zero incremental upkeep.
unknowns: Local duty coverage and student assistance needs
research_questions: Where does the duty rota leave insufficient supervision?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100, gross0 and net0. No physical supervision or assistance is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Sponsor extracurricular clubs, student organizations and academic contests

steps.what: Agree accessible extracurricular goals, activity choices and participation needs with students
Prepare club logistics and approve dates, accessibility arrangements and student invitations
Sponsor activities, support student leadership and supervise safe and inclusive participation

tasks.design: Use recurring activity templates in {CALENDAR} and {DOCS} to reduce logistics preparation. The teacher captures the brief and checks each invitation before release, then retains live sponsorship and supervision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recurring events require repeated logistics entry alongside substantial relationship work.
tasks.enabler_now: Native recurring schedules and reusable invitations handle stable logistics.
tasks.still_hard: Inclusive participation, student leadership and safe supervision.
tasks.human_edge: Adapting activities to students' interests and support needs.
tasks.altitude: A little less logistics preparation; student-facing sponsorship remains intact.

reach.learn: Accessible event planning and booking constraints

evidence.claim: Recurring calendars and reusable invitations support logistics configuration; task savings are E1 assumptions.

assumptions: Boundary includes activity agreement, logistics and direct sponsorship; no separate whole-school scheduling work is counted.
Teacher produces activity, dates, recipients, location and access requirements in retained s1 and s2; s2's 12.5 remaining hours include first capture and exact invitation approval.
Test native calendar features first; unsupported bookings and changed student needs are handled manually in s2.
Two incremental hours per 100 baseline hours cover template and recipient-list maintenance.
unknowns: Event frequency, access arrangements and existing calendar features
research_questions: How much logistics time remains after first capture and invitation checks?

already_counted.description: Logistics capture, exceptions and invitation approval

approvals.approved_version: Exact dates, location, access arrangements, invitation text and recipients; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R87.5; gross12.5 minus2 upkeep gives10.5 net. Irregular events may save only2 logistics hours, leaving zero net; live sponsorship stays60.

role.altitude: Preserve direct support and supervision while reducing supported Braille transcription and recurring logistics.
reach: Coordinate accessible materials with a specialist
Align club facilities with the activities coordinator
role.ambitious_version: More accessible extracurricular participation with unchanged student safety and interpretation responsibility.
